programme.desc: Amanda and Mandy try every trick in the book to help a snared hyena, a lion threatens a village, and the team's plan to release a troop of 13 monkeys is thwarted by last-minute surgery and some crafty escape artists.

programme.title: Kenya Wildlife Diaries
programme.desc: Lewa Conservancy is working to return elephants to territory from Mt Kenya to Samburu National Park. They have also created an elephant exclusion zone to try to restore a damaged ecosystem.

programme.title: High Life in the Dead Mountains
Shark: British Isles Special with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve explores a world of sharks right on your doorstep. Meet everything from Basking sharks to Angelsharks which have never been filmed before, and discover the threats these sharks face.

programme.title: Wild Dogs
programme.desc: Discover the ways in which natural selection and human pressure have shaped the raccoon dog, the golden jackal and the maned wolf.

programme.title: Ol Pejeta Diaries
programme.desc: A once-in-a-generation drought has sucked all the moisture from surrounding rivers and the Conservation team is struggling to keep up with the swath of thirsty creatures.

programme.title: Ol Pejeta Diaries
programme.desc: Eco-tourism isn't just a background player in the operation of Ol Pej, it's the financial backbone that keeps the park operating. From comfortable camping to ulta-luxurious accommodations, the guests that stay at Ol Pejeta live among nature.

programme.title: Malawi Wildlife Rescue
programme.desc: Amanda and Mandy try every trick in the book to help a snared hyena, a lion threatens a village, and the team's plan to release a troop of 13 monkeys is thwarted by last-minute surgery and some crafty escape artists.

programme.title: Kenya Wildlife Diaries
programme.desc: Lewa Conservancy is working to return elephants to territory from Mt Kenya to Samburu National Park. They have also created an elephant exclusion zone to try to restore a damaged ecosystem.

programme.title: Africa's Wild Horizons
programme.desc: An immense, dry land dominates southwestern Africa. Here, sand covers the land in rippling dunes and rain drains away as quickly as it falls. Kalahari, meaning place of great thirst, is an appropriate name for one of southern Africa's greatest wildernesses.

programme.title: Big Cats: An Amazing Animal Family
programme.desc: As Patrick Aryee delves into the feline family tree, he witnesses gravity-defying 'catrobatics', tests a cheetah's speed and explores the odd-looking Pallas's cat.

programme.title: Wild Wild East
programme.desc: In Hampton, New Brunswick the deer population is running wild. In the summer locals struggle to maintain their crops from growing fawns and hungry does. Sightings are common and residents fear the overpopulation may be at its tipping point.

programme.title: Wild Wild East
programme.desc: Brier Island is at the western point of the Bay of Fundy in Nova Scotia. In the surrounding waters live an incredible number of humpback whales and dolphins. On still waters, Humpbacks smash their tails, flap their fins, and breach one en masse.

programme.title: The Living Beach
programme.desc: Just beyond Australia's Queensland State is Fraser Island, a complex ecosystem built entirely upon sand. In the middle of its rainforests, eucalyptus woodlands and mangrove forests, a visitor to Fraser Island is always standing upon the living beach.

programme.title: The Living Beach
programme.desc: The beaches of California are some of the most beautiful in the world, but they are falling out of balance due to mankind's effects on nature. We ask what can be done to stop this.

programme.title: Alaskan Summer
programme.desc: The effects of summer weather on Alaskan wildlife.

programme.title: Animal Senses
programme.desc: The first sense to evolve in the first animals was chemoreception. It means being able to detect chemicals in the animal's environment. This helps animals find prey and mates, and to sense predators from a distance.

programme.title: Animal Senses
programme.desc: The sense of touch is useful to feel physical forces such as bites, changes in temperature and texture. Some animals have become extra sensitive to feel very faint vibrations, which give them a lot of information about their environment.

programme.title: Animal Senses
programme.desc: Seeing the world is one of the most amazing animal adaptations. Different types of eyes give animals different types of vision, and in some cases they can be extraordinary.

programme.title: Animal Senses
programme.desc: Sound waves are produced by movement. Animals have evolved organs to detect those sound waves in the air or water to perceive movements in their environment. This can be used to find prey, predators, and mates. These are some of the animals that have mastered the sense of hearing.

programme.title: Superbeast
programme.desc: Celebrate nature's ultimate athletes as they survive, excel and dominate in Earth's toughest arenas. From apex predators to cunning creatures, go full Superbeast.

programme.title: Slovenia: Where Nature Comes First
programme.desc: The filmmaker sheds light on the captivating nature, wildlife and landscapes in Slovenia, where humans have learnt how to coexist with nature without affecting its beauty.

programme.title: David Attenborough's Dragons And Damsels
programme.desc: They are beautiful, their behaviours are as complex as mammals and they have existed since the dinosaurs. Join David Attenborough as he delves into the life of dragonflies and damselflies.

programme.title: Kingdom of Plants
programme.desc: David begins his journey inside the magnificent Palm House, a unique global rainforest in London.

programme.title: Kingdom of Plants
programme.desc: David Attenborough explores the secret life of plants at Kew, examining everything from a huge underground specimen to a snappy carnivorous variety.

programme.title: Kingdom of Plants
programme.desc: David Attenborough concludes his absorbing journey around London's Kew Gardens, as he discovers how some plants have evolved to shed their dependency on water enabling them to survive in the driest environments.

programme.title: Wild Dogs: Pack vs. Pride
programme.desc: The Kakumbi see a leopard who's been stalking them, Julz goes fishing with Simon, explores mealtime pack hierarchy and witnesses a heartbreaking vigil for a badly injured Kakumbi pup.

programme.title: Wild Dogs: Pack vs. Pride
programme.desc: Heading back to the den with the Kakumbi who are mourning the loss of two pups. A look at a hyena den and lion pride trying to take down a buffalo and catching up with the Manzi who are in a standoff with a leopard and a herd of angry elephants.

programme.title: Wolves & Lions: Old Enemies
programme.desc: Ancient Enemies: In Africa, lions and wolves lead their ecosystems. Discover the strength, social strategies and hierarchies behind how they raise and protect their young.

programme.title: Pride Rules
programme.desc: Say hello to a season of plenty as flood waters recede and vast herds of prey return to the Chobe's banks. Watch Keeza and her cub make a break for it.

programme.title: Matsalu Moose: Wild Giants of the Baltics
programme.desc: Matsalu Bay in the Baltic Sea is an important stopover for migrating birds and home to many rare plant and animal species. For most of the year, moose roam the marshes and plains of Matsalu, which is a nature reserve and under strict protection.

programme.title: Wild Dogs: Pack vs. Pride
programme.desc: The Kakumbi see a leopard who's been stalking them, Julz goes fishing with Simon, explores mealtime pack hierarchy and witnesses a heartbreaking vigil for a badly injured Kakumbi pup.

programme.title: Wolves & Lions: Old Enemies

programme.title: Ocean's Greatest Feast
programme.desc: Get a front-row seat to the planet's biggest biomass migration, as billions of sardines migrate along South Africa's east coast, each hoping to escape the jaws of hungry predators.

programme.title: Great Lakes Wild
programme.desc: The Lake Erie Watersnake is currently on the brink of extinction, and researchers have been fighting to get it back. And it looks like it's finally working - thanks to the round goby. Grad student Lizzy Mack is heading out on day trips to catch bucket loads of the snakes, collect measurements, and inject them with small microchips to track them along their way, all while dodging bites from some of the crankiest snakes around.

programme.title: Great Lakes Wild
programme.desc: Where animals and humans co-exist, how do you stop a bad reputation from pushing a species towards extinction? From Rattlesnakes to Cormorants, see how creatures that have bad reputations are bring dealt with when it comes to conservation.
